clue.text: Mean to acquire a sort of square cupboard

parts.note: close means mean or stingy with money
a T-square is a drawing tool, so T is a sort of square

explanation.surface: A miser sets out to buy a square-shaped cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like a verb (intend), but it is the adjective, stingy; 'to acquire' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A small room or cabinet for storing clothes and goods is a cupboard by another name.

clue.text: It grows almost like Akela

indicators.note: almost means the word stops just short of its last letter

parts.note: Akela is the wolf in The Jungle Book, so like Akela means wolfish, lupine

explanation.surface: Something growing looks almost like the Cub Scout leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Akela is both the wolf leader in Kipling's Jungle Book and the title of a Cub Scout leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden flower bearing tall spikes is something that grows.

clue.text: Bloomer made by a certain councillor during stay

indicators.note: during places the other pieces inside the stay

parts.note: to stay is to stop
a certain one, so ONE

explanation.surface: A local politician blunders while staying somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a blunder; it means a plant that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A succulent with yellow or pink flowers growing on rocks is a flowering plant.

clue.text: Somehow contrive to make a metal stand

indicators.note: somehow here signals that the answer is concealed somehow within the next words

explanation.surface: Someone manages to craft a metal stand.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer lies inside 'conTRIVE To'; 'contrive' tempts as an anagram but its letters do not fit.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-legged iron rest for pots by the fire is a metal stand.

clue.text: Sucker going to pot

parts.note: something that has gone or is going is off, as in departed
to pot an animal is to shoot it

explanation.surface: A gullible person is heading for ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sucker' reads as a dupe and 'going to pot' as decay; in fact a sucker is a gardening term for a shoot from a plant's root, and pot means shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: A sucker in botany is a side growth springing from a plant's base, a kind of side branch.

clue.text: Exultant, unlike criminals and their associates?

definitions.meaning: criminals inhabit the underworld, so the opposite is to be above it

explanation.definitionFit: Elated people feel high above everything, and those above are the reverse of the underworld.

clue.text: Notes and not so anonymous

parts.note: face value is printed on banknotes; face is the obverse of notes
less means not so much

explanation.surface: Banknotes and less anonymity.
explanation.definitionFit: Without identity, lacking a known face, describes an unnamed person.

clue.text: Cry "——! and let slip the dogs of war" (V Caesar)

definitions.text: Cry "——! and let slip the dogs of war" (V Caesar)

parts.words: Cry "——! and let slip the dogs of war" (V Caesar)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank from Mark Antony's speech in Shakespeare's Julius Caesar, Act III

explanation.definitionFit: The cry was a signal to soldiers for slaughter and plunder, meaning chaos.

clue.text: Concerned with deliveries involving bistro, etc

indicators.note: involving here means the letters are entangled and rearranged

explanation.surface: A matter of delivering food to a bistro and the like.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deliveries' sounds like couriers; it means childbirth. 'involving' rearranges BISTRO ETC.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to childbirth and midwifery means dealing with births.

clue.text: Haiti's crop — uncommonly pithy

indicators.note: uncommonly suggests the letters are arranged in an unusual way

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive S counted here as a letter

explanation.surface: A remark that Haiti's harvest is unusually terse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncommonly' tells you to rearrange the ten letters of HAITIS CROP.
explanation.definitionFit: Pithy speech is concise and full of maxims, the style of a writer of aphorisms.

clue.text: Nobleman given a travel permit

parts.note: Vis. is an abbreviation for viscount, a nobleman
taken as written

explanation.surface: A peer is handed his travel papers.
explanation.definitionFit: An endorsement in a passport allowing entry to a country is a permit to travel.

clue.text: Reportedly require a lot in Bow, to be so immersed

indicators.note: reportedly means we hear the words spoken rather than read them

parts.note: require a lot is need heap; Bow is in London's East End, where Cockneys drop the H, so it becomes need 'eap

explanation.surface: Someone in east London needs plenty in order to be fully absorbed.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is a district of London's East End; the Cockney accent drops the H of heap, so NEED 'EAP sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Deeply involved, as if water came up to one's legs' joints, is being thus immersed.

clue.text: Servant's song about king in church

indicators.note: about means the song wraps round the rest

parts.note: a lay is a song or ballad

indicators.note: in places the king letter inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A servant has a song about a king in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Servant's' is the definition plus 's for has; 'song' tempts as the definition, but it supplies the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A footman or menial attendant is a liveried servant.

clue.text: Ogle lasciviously when part of film is run back

indicators.note: is run back, like rewinding film, means read the word backwards

parts.note: a reel is one spool, a part of a film

explanation.surface: A viewer leers at a sequence when the projector rewinds it.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone a sly, lustful look is to ogle them.

clue.text: Person displaying one in her box, it turns out

indicators.note: turns out means the letters are turned about into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone shows off a thing in her box, and so it proves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns out' rearranges I with HER BOX IT; 'in' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who shows work at a fair or gallery is one who displays it.

clue.text: Place producing food that can be smelt?

definitions.text: Place producing food that can be smelt?

parts.words: Place producing food that can be smelt?
parts.note: smelt seems to be the past tense of smell, but a smelt is a small fish, so the place rears fish for food

explanation.definitionFit: Ponds or tanks where fish are bred for eating are an aquaculture site.

clue.text: Time taken by sound man to shore up stronghold

indicators.note: in a down entry shoring up means sitting below and supporting the stronghold

parts.note: a fort is a stronghold

indicators.note: sound means the word is heard, not written

parts.note: a knight is a chess man

explanation.surface: A period spent by a healthy man propping up a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound man' reads as a healthy man; 'sound' is the homophone signal for KNIGHT, a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Two weeks is a span of time.

clue.text: God protecting painting is biased

indicators.note: protecting means the god surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild
painting is art
taken as written

explanation.surface: A deity guarding a picture is partial.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking one side, being a partisan, means being prejudiced.

clue.text: Blow for stylish student wearing thin coat

indicators.note: wearing means the coat goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a wash is a thin coat of paint
hip means fashionable or stylish
L is a learner driver, so a student

explanation.surface: A fashionable learner in a flimsy coat takes a hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A lashing stroke, as of a lash, is a blow; also a neck injury from a jolt.

clue.text: Firm support for a diamond

definitions.meaning: slang for a gem, especially a diamond

explanation.definitionFit: Solid stone gives firm support, and slang calls a diamond this.

clue.text: A Frenchman's means of travelling to college

parts.note: BR is British Rail, a means of travelling
Eton is the famous English school

explanation.surface: A Frenchman travels to a college by some means.
explanation.walkthrough: BR was British Rail, the UK's national railway; ETON is England's famous boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Brittany is from a region of France.

clue.text: Former pupil in 5 ac's books is a noted player

annotationWithheld.why: Former pupil in S ac's books is a noted player (6): OB + O(IS)T fits, but the scan prints 'S ac's' (or '5 ac's') which neither builds letters nor links; garbled print
annotationWithheld.clue: Former pupil in 5 ac's books is a noted player

clue.text: Order having superhuman powers, though not the first born

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: bionic means enhanced with superhuman powers

explanation.surface: A society of the gifted, though not of those born first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' is a column style in architecture; 'though' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A classical column style with scroll capitals is an architectural order.

clue.text: Swears in broadcast to get attention

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone curses on air to get noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: Watchful caution is a heedful kind of attention.

clue.text: Girl standing up to embrace island's rope-maker

indicators.note: to embrace means the girl goes round the island letter
in a down entry standing up means the word reads upwards

parts.note: a lass is a girl
I is short for island

explanation.surface: A girl rises to hug an island rope-maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing up' turns LASS into SSAL; I goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The agave fibre is used for cord, so it makes rope.

clue.text: Astonish by almost completing a daring manoeuvre

indicators.note: almost means the word falls short of its last letter

parts.note: a stunt is a daring feat

explanation.surface: A performer amazes by nearly completing a risky trick.
explanation.definitionFit: To stagger or daze with surprise is to astonish.

clue.text: General rejected schemes, soldier being involved in trial

indicators.note: rejected, like something sent back, means the word is read backwards

parts.note: arts are wiles or schemes

indicators.note: being involved in means the soldier goes inside the trial

parts.note: a test is a trial
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A general turned down plans while a soldier was on trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns the schemes word backwards to STRA. 'General' looks like an adjective or a rank; it is a planner of campaigns.
explanation.definitionFit: A military commander is a planner of campaigns, so a general is a tactician.

clue.text: Prepared chard in a tick, perhaps

indicators.note: prepared food is worked over, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Chard cooked in a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a tick' looks like a moment of time; it is the eight-legged parasite. 'Prepared' rearranges CHARD IN A.
explanation.definitionFit: Ticks are eight-legged, like spiders and mites, members of that class.

clue.text: Cause annoyance in the plant

definitions.meaning: a stinging weed with hairy leaves

explanation.definitionFit: To irritate someone and a stinging weed share this name.
